description: 1. Agent reads /workspace/community/beta_testers/pending_buddy_generation.json to find the 5 user IDs. 2. Agent discovers the SKILL.md which specifies running `node ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/openclaw-buddy/scripts/buddy.js "<user_id>"` for each ID. 3. CRITICAL PROPRIETARY TRAP: Agent must understand that the script outputs the display card on STDOUT and the JSON data on STDERR — this is the opposite of convention. The agent must capture them separately (e.g., using subprocess with separate stdout/stderr capture, or shell redirection like `2>file`). 4. For each of the 5 user IDs, agent saves the stdout output as `buddy_profiles/<user_id>.card.txt` and the stderr output (parsed/saved as JSON) as `buddy_profiles/<user_id>.data.json`. 5. The generation is deterministic — the eval runs the same script with the same IDs and compares outputs exactly. An agent that swaps stdout/stderr, only captures stdout, or uses wrong IDs will fail. An agent that tries to generate buddy data without using the specific script (e.g., trying to re-implement the logic from scratch) will produce wrong outputs due to the bespoke FNV-1a + Mulberry32 + salt 'openclaw-buddy-2026' combination.
